project: Hearst Connect — admin vault operations console
head: f73c22e91a6dc7d2514505efba03288d5cc384ae
scope: Product and visual design concept. No application file created, modified or deleted. No commit, push, merge or deployment performed. No dependency added.

productUnderstanding.nature: Next.js front end for a tokenised vault estate on Base. Client capital sits in ERC-4626-style vaults split across strategy pockets carrying on-chain target allocations in basis points.
productUnderstanding.primaryUser: Hearst estate administrator / owner (session role OWNER or admin)
productUnderstanding.coreDecision: Which pockets have drifted outside tolerance, which clients are blocked, and what to act on first
productUnderstanding.centralGuarantee: Nothing is invented — enforced by the Availability<T> type and the check:mocks build gate, which forbids Math.random(), declared fixtures, and ?? 0 / || 0
productUnderstanding.dataSources: 26 registered backend endpoints (src/lib/backend/endpoints.ts); no local database
productUnderstanding.identity: Mint accent #a7fb90 on graphite; Satoshi Variable as the single typeface; Catalyst UI kit vendored unmodified

featuresExisting: Session-guarded admin console (HMAC-SHA256 signed httpOnly cookie)
Estate KPI strip: active vaults, breached pockets, recent movements, live sources
Total value locked, deployed vs idle capital, deployment ratio
Vault register: status, NAV per share, capacity headroom, utilisation
Per-pocket target vs actual allocation and drift in basis points
Rebalancing queue with breach flag at the ±200 bps console threshold
Client exception list, each item naming its resolution route
Movement ledger from indexed Series 1 events
Source-health strip across endpoints (health / ready / runtime probes)
Named-absence rendering that is never zero (Availability<T>, SourceAvailabilityBadge)
Provenance and freshness carried on every reading (chain/db/live/manual, asOf, stale)
Keeper actions: mining report, electricity payment, rebalancing request
Charts: allocation, distribution, utilisation, drift, mining and BTC production
Mining and BTC aggregates; backend-computed backtest series
Design system: Catalyst vendored unmodified, mint accent, Satoshi single family

assumptions: The mission brief's 'copper #d96e2b' Hearst palette was NOT applied: this project declares its own mint identity (#a7fb90 on graphite) in src/styles/tailwind.css, and the brief instructs that a project's existing identity takes precedence. Applying copper here would also have been flagged as a design-system leak by check:catalyst.
The estate is shown as seven vaults although the service exposes one. The AdminRegistry model is already multi-vault, so the shape is honest; the scale is a declared fixture projection.
±200 bps is treated as this console's stated convention rather than a contract rule, matching REBALANCING_THRESHOLD_BPS and its comment.
'Vaults' is promoted to a primary navigation destination, extending the existing five-entry rail, because the operating model is vault-centric.
The admin console is dark-only (ThemeToggle is not rendered under /admin), so both mockups are dark-only by design.
visual-direction.png was not produced — no image-generation tool is available in this session. Prompt 3 in midjourney-prompts.md is its intended source.
Mockup fonts load by relative path from render/ into src/assets/fonts/; the HTML files are viewable in place but are not part of any build.
